summary: An excerpt from a novel (Book 10, part 79) in which Ms. McCavity receives an unannounced visit from Damian Feinstein, who is fumbling and earnest, while a young embedded reporter shadows her. Damian reports that Senator Rittenhouse, a powerful committee chairman tied to network operators, wants a bill moved from Judiciary to Commerce and called hearings, which McCavity judges a delay rather than a killing of the bill. Damian invites her to represent the other side in a post-mortem debate that evening, and she plans to handle him carefully.
one_line: In a novel excerpt, McCavity dismisses reporters and hears from Damian Feinstein that Senator Rittenhouse is delaying a bill, then agrees to debate him.
key_facts: Damian Feinstein greets Ms. McCavity with a long, intense handshake that draws stares from journalists and a think-tank man.
Damian's curly hair is gelled into a configuration that reminds McCavity of the glossy ringlets of a black poodle.
McCavity triages her visitors by deadline and promises to meet the think-tank man for dinner at an Ethiopian place in Adams-Morgan.
McCavity leads Damian into her office accompanied by a very young, very bright embedded reporter who is her shadow for the duration.
Damian says the bill is dead, citing a personal call from Senator Rittenhouse.
Senator Rittenhouse takes the position that the bill should be in Commerce, not Judiciary, and is calling hearings to make that happen.
Rittenhouse is described as another powerful committee chairman who has been in the pocket of the network operators for a decade.
Editorialists and talk-radio types call Rittenhouse "The Senator from The Internet."
McCavity says the Commerce referral is a far cry from killing the bill and is pretty standard, just slowing things down.
Damian's press-liaison has set up a post-mortem debate on one of the news networks that evening.
Damian invites McCavity to represent the other side in the debate.
McCavity thinks Damian is twice the rhetorician she is but has no idea how to play the game, so she must bruise him without breaking him.
Damian says, "We, as a society, make trade-offs all the time."
